co_look_at_me_wall.blurb: Look At Me! Wall is a small roadside cliff beside Rampart Range Road in the South Platte country, around 8,400 feet, with a view down Williams Canyon toward Pikes Peak. It holds eleven climbs, nearly all bolted sport lines plus a single trad route. Grades bunch around 5.10, with a handful of 5.11s and one 5.9. The gneiss is a touch loose in places but good overall, and the routes share a similar feel while each has its own twist. There is almost no walk, which makes it an easy add-on to a day along the road.

co_middle_class_wall.blurb: Middle Class Wall is part of the Triple Tier area in Poudre Canyon, along Colorado Highway 14 near Fort Collins, at about 6,200 feet. It faces north-northwest, so it stays shaded and works well on hot summer days. The eleven routes are mostly bolted sport lines with one gear route, roughly 60 to 100 feet tall, climbing a lower slabby section and then a steeper headwall. Expect stiff grades, mostly 5.11 and 5.12 with a couple of easier lines and one harder. A short third-class scramble over flakes gets you to the ledge at the base.

co_lover_s_leap_on_beaver_brook.blurb: Lover's Leap on Beaver Brook is a small cluster of eleven climbs above Golden, reached on foot from Windy Saddle Park off Lookout Mountain Road. Most lines are single-pitch bolted sport routes, joined by a few trad lines, a top-rope and one boulder problem. Grades start easy and run mostly through 5.8 to 5.11, with one much harder line. The hike in is a bit over a mile and a half and takes under an hour, so this is a modest morning outing near Denver rather than a drive-up crag.
co_lover_s_leap_on_beaver_brook.parking_note: Leave the car in the main lot at Windy Saddle Park, a little under a mile past the switchbacks on Lookout Mountain Road above Golden.

co_pratt_s_rock_aka_pratt_s_overhang.blurb: Pratt's Rock, also called Pratt's Overhang, is a compact bouldering spot on Flagstaff Mountain above Boulder, close to the Monkey Traverse. A small, slightly overhanging face split by a crack gives most of the interest, and the place carries a lot of local history for its size. The eleven problems are mostly in the V0 to V4 range, then jump to a few hard sit-start and variation lines from V7 up to V11. Flagstaff stone has a rough, sandpapery feel that wears skin, so expect powerful moves on abrasive holds.
